stories.title: How AI is changing the nature of cyberattacks
stories.why: AI may be helping cyberattackers increase the speed and scale of their operations, but it is not yet changing their core objectives or the techniques they employ as part of their attack chains.

stories.title: AI-written patches are becoming attack maps for hackers
stories.why: This summer, the maintainers of vm2, an open-source JavaScript sandboxing library with 1 million downloads per week, shipped fixes for 34 separate sandbox-escape vulnerabilities and Anthropic’s Claude co-wrote 19 of…

stories.title: The firewall becomes the foothold: Attackers turn Check Point gateways against customers
stories.why: A firewall is intended to be a boundary attackers can’t cross.

stories.title: The benign true positive: When trusted AI agents look like attackers
stories.why: A coding agent opens hundreds of files, launches command-line tools and connects to an internal service to complete a task.

stories.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
stories.why: Attackers' AI agents have been hunting for weak spots in internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify to steal the AI provider keys stored inside, according to the agents' own records.

stories.title: AI uncovers flaws in discontinued devices with no vendor left to patch them
stories.why: Forescout researchers built a tool to test if generally available AI models could find security flaws on a limited budget.

stories.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
stories.why: The compromise of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace was the result of the theft of an access key that was exposed in the wake of a breach targeting Fireworks AI.

stories.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole Over $400 Million in Crypto Using Deepfake Video Calls
FBI Highlights Growing Abuse of AI-Driven Pentesting Framework ARTEX
stories.why: The FBI warns that threat actors are increasingly using open-source AI pentesting tool ARTEX to launch fast, large-scale intrusions worldwide

stories.title: AI Cuts Vulnerability Discovery from Nine Months to 90 Hours
stories.why: Forescout report claims to have found 66 new flaws in just 90 hours using AI
